title: Chassis Design, Welding and Fabrication
author: Erudior
description: Compare unibody, ladder-frame and spaceframe structures, choose materials and joints, then fabricate and inspect a structural teaching bay. Includes a parts atlas and an assessed modification workshop.
changelog: Added an individual parts atlas, hands-on modification workshop, instance-level build ledger and pre/post verification.

lessons.title: Trace a load through a frame bay
lessons.body:
Entry skills: complete Workshop Measurement and Vehicle Service, Brake, Steering and Suspension Service, or demonstrate the equivalent workshop skills.

A chassis carries loads from suspension, powertrain, restraints and body mounts. Sketch forces from the point of application to supporting nodes. A pinned rectangular frame can rack. A diagonal provides an axial load path, although real joints and joints in bending still need calculation and testing. Stiffness describes deflection under load. Strength and fatigue life are separate design questions.

## Worked shop case

Two equal frames move 3 mm and 6 mm under the same small fixture load. The first frame has twice the test stiffness under that loading. These data give no ultimate strength or fatigue rating.

## Guided practice

A bench frame deflects 2 mm under 100 N in a small-deflection test. What is its stiffness in N/mm?

Predict the result, then use the first quiz item to check your reasoning.

**What you will produce.** A fabricated bay, its jig, inspected coupons and an as-built dimensional report.

Identify individual components in the parts atlas and trace their interfaces on your exact donor drawing.

lessons.title: Body-on-frame, unibody and triangulated spaceframes
lessons.body:
Follow loads from the contact patches into the suspension pickups, then through the structure to the supported masses. A ladder frame uses longitudinal rails and crossmembers with a body attached through mounts. A unibody distributes loads through joined floor, sills, pillars, bulkheads and panels. Removing a seemingly minor panel can interrupt a structural path. A tubular spaceframe can take loads through triangulated members when pickup loads reach nodes and joints behave as designed. Bending still occurs under off-node loads, local eccentricity and real boundary conditions.

Compare stiffness, crash-management provisions, corrosion protection, joint inspection, repair access, occupant protection and mass for a stated use. Material strength, stiffness and fatigue resistance are different properties. A stiff frame can still have an unsafe joint. Never infer crashworthiness from a torsion rig or a visually straight frame. For the learner-built car, record who reviewed each structural design and what evidence qualified it for the intended operation.

## Worked shop case

A pickup on an unbraced tube midspan adds bending that a pin-jointed truss model at a node would miss. Trace both load and reaction, update the model and request joint review before fabrication. A student bay can test build accuracy and load-deflection behavior within a reviewed fixture. Its result does not qualify a complete chassis.

## Guided practice

```example fade=2
problem: A fixture twists 2 degrees under 400 N·m at its stated boundary conditions. How would you compare a second bay?
step: Compute stiffness as torque divided by angle.
step: Hold supports, load and measurement points constant.
answer: The first result is 200 N·m per degree; compare the second under the same conditions and account for fixture compliance.
```

## Independent shop or design task

Trace front suspension and seat-belt loads on two candidate chassis drawings. Identify nodes, mounting pads, access to inspect the back side, corrosion traps and where a qualified reviewer must establish acceptance.

Record the selected component, alternative, source and measured result in your component record. Identify open items for the design or practical reviewer.

lessons.title: Steel, aluminum, composites and their joints
topics: Steel, aluminum, composites and their joints
lessons.body:
Mild steel sheet is formable and often joinable by familiar processes. Advanced high-strength steel grades can be heat-sensitive and require location-specific repair instructions. Aluminum alloys differ in temper and weldability; joining can change local properties. A composite laminate carries loads according to fiber direction, matrix and ply schedule. Impact damage or delamination can be hard to see. Choose an identified grade or laminate schedule, thickness, joining process, corrosion control and inspection method together.

A welded seam can transmit continuous load but introduces heat, distortion and a heat-affected zone. Rivets and bolts transfer load through bearing, shear, tension or clamp friction as designed. An adhesive distributes load over an area but depends on surface preparation, temperature, cure, joint geometry and peel exposure. Dissimilar conductive materials in an electrolyte can corrode galvanically. A higher-strength bolt or thicker plate alone does not validate the joint, surrounding structure or crash behavior.

## Worked shop case

An aluminum outer panel and steel support fit geometrically. The specified procedure uses an isolating adhesive, sealed edges and coated fasteners. A bare metal direct joint could introduce a corrosion path even if it fits more neatly. Record the source for material identity, required preparation, cure and physical inspection access.

## Guided practice

```example fade=2
problem: Two bonded coupons carry the same load but one sees edge peel. Should equal bonded area imply equal capacity?
step: Identify how load enters each bond.
step: Check the documented lap-shear and peel geometry, materials and cure.
answer: Equal area can distribute stress very differently. Test approved coupons and avoid inferring structural equivalence.
```

## Independent shop or design task

Make nonstructural sample joints under the shop's approved process. Identify parent material, joint geometry, preparation, settings or cure conditions, and inspected result. Record where the selected vehicle build needs a different qualified procedure.

Record the selected component, alternative, source and measured result in your component record. Identify open items for the design or practical reviewer.

lessons.title: Dimension from datums and plan inspection access
lessons.body:
Define three reference planes, label longitudinal stations and set one dimension origin. Give the fixture a way to locate tubes without over-constraining the assembly. Locate critical mount coordinates independently of overall diagonal checks. Plan inspection access before covering welds or installing panels.

## Worked shop case

A 300 by 400 mm rectangular fixture has a nominal 500 mm diagonal. Equal diagonals are a quick rack check. Both diagonals can still be equal if the fixture was built to the wrong size.

## Guided practice

A rectangular 600 by 800 mm fixture should have which nominal diagonal in mm?

Predict the result, then use the first quiz item to check your reasoning.

## Your design

Choose a bay from a documented design or a chassis engineer's reviewed concept. Mark three datums, simple load paths, wheel and seat reference locations, tolerances, tool access and a fixture inspection sequence. Identify where the structural reviewer must approve the proposed use.

```assignment
writing: design
```

## Component design review

Compare the candidates in the component register and bring your selected configuration into this design.

```assignment
writing: component-selection
```

Read a modification card, choose a baseline and identify the changed parts, including hardware and seals.

lessons.title: Make a jig and a representative welded bay
lessons.body:
Select traceable material from a reviewed design. Record section, alloy, thickness and joining process. Practice on coupons of the same material and joint type; have the welding instructor evaluate fit and joints before structural fabrication. Clamp the bay to identified stops, verify dimensions at tack stage and remeasure after cooling. Do structural work under the reviewed procedure.

## Worked shop case

A tack-stage width is 400.0 mm. After joining and cooling it is 399.1 mm. The recorded change is 0.9 mm, and the part must be dispositioned against its drawing tolerance.

## Guided practice

Target width is 450.0 mm. Cooled width is 448.8 mm. Give the magnitude of the error in mm.

Predict the result, then use the first quiz item to check your reasoning.

## US rules at the workbench

Covered workplaces must address machine guarding (29 CFR 1910.212) and hot-work fire and exposure controls (1910.252). Use the shop's hot-work authorization where applicable and document ventilation, combustibles, PPE, guarding and the responsible reviewer before making sparks. Check local fire, occupancy and zoning requirements for your own workshop. Retain material and joint inspection records.

[OSHA — welding, cutting and brazing, 29 CFR 1910.252](https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.252/) · [OSHA — machine guarding, 29 CFR 1910.212](https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.212) · [OSHA — PPE, 29 CFR 1910.132](https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.132) · [OSHA — workers and establishments covered](https://www.osha.gov/node/59586)

## Workshop preparation

Only weld under a qualified shop's hot-work controls with appropriate local exhaust, PPE and fire precautions. Never weld on containers or structures with fuel or unknown residues. Keep prototype parts out of vehicle use until reviewed.

```assignment
lab: workshop
```

Bring the selected component record to the lab and enter what you personally inspected, made, measured or assembled, with the part identifier and actual conditions.

lessons.title: Make a drawing someone else can inspect
topics: Make a drawing someone else can inspect
lessons.body:
Open the parts atlas for this system. Trace a parent assembly into its named children and mounting hardware. Explain the function of each item, identify its controlling dimensions or interfaces, then decide which pieces you can machine or fabricate, which you can assemble and which to obtain as qualified assemblies. Put exact drawing or donor references beside your decision.

## Parts on the bench

Primary structure, joints and attachment hardware, Mounting and underbody protection. The quick references linked below include the function, design, fabrication or installation route, and verification of every indexed item.

## Modifications to evaluate

- Bolt-on chassis brace
- Serviceable undertray

## Worked example

A teaching bracket's two hole centers are nominally 40.0 mm apart. A direct center-spacing tolerance of ±0.5 mm makes 40.4 acceptable and 40.7 a rework. If both holes instead have ±0.5 mm independent position dimensions from an edge, the worst-case separation error is ±1.0 mm. Specify the functional distance directly.

## Guided decision

```example fade=1
problem: A bracket fits only after bending the cables around its cut edge. Which design item was missed?
step: Check edge condition, protected clearance and cable bend radius with the actual connector fitted.
answer: Revise the route or bracket and inspect the measured assembly before adding it to the build.
```

## Independent workshop

Make the two-hole nonstructural service plate in the bench plans, log each manufactured and purchased part, and test removal and refit.

Open a modification card for its design, build and test sequence. Record original and changed readings under comparable conditions. Separate physical evidence from predictions and document a safe rollback.

```assignment
writing: modification-record
```

lessons.title: Document an as-built bay
lessons.body:
Compare coordinates, diagonals, joint condition and material traceability to the reviewed drawing. Have an appropriate reviewer inspect welds and select applicable nondestructive or destructive tests. Keep a nonconforming part quarantined until disposition is documented. A coupon test and an unloaded bay mock-up answer narrower questions than vehicle-level durability or occupant protection.

## Worked shop case

A representative brace passes a coupon check but the actual belt mount has no load review. Log the coupon result under joining and carry the belt mount as a separate unresolved requirement.

## Guided practice

An allowed fixture interval is 299.5–300.5 mm. A reading of 300.8 mm exceeds its upper limit by how many mm?

Predict the result, then use the first quiz item to check your reasoning.

## Practical sign-off

The physically fabricated bay, coupon record and datum-based measurements can be traced to one drawing revision. Record actual measurements and the disposition of faults. Submit the physical evidence in the workshop record.

```assignment
lab: workshop
```

Close each build-relevant component row with its measured result, reviewer disposition or an identified open issue and retest. Transfer the accepted configuration to your capstone record.

Reconcile required, issued, installed and verified quantities against the physical assembly and mark unresolved items.

references.title: Component register and build evidence
references.body:
For this course examine Primary chassis; Material and structural joint; Mounts and fasteners. Document manufacturer, part revision, drawing, selection, applicable authority or service requirement, installer, measured result with units, and reviewer disposition. Begin in design and update after installation.

| Family | Candidate designs | What changes | What to verify |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Primary chassis | Unibody / ladder frame / triangulated spaceframe | Trace static, fatigue and occupant loads to actual structural paths. | Provide reviewed drawings, datum survey and measured fixture results. |
| Material and structural joint | Mild or advanced steel / aluminum / composite; weld / fastener / adhesive | Heat, cure, galvanic isolation and local load direction affect each joint. | Record material traceability, coupon results, joining procedure and inspection. |
| Mounts and fasteners | Rigid / compliant mounts; bolted / studded or welded attachments | Clamp load, joint stiffness, movement and service removability interact. | Document fastener spec, torque procedure, witness marking and isolation at interfaces. |

references.title: Primary structure, joints and attachment hardware · Frame rail to Weld joint
references.body:
For an actual vehicle, identify the exact model, part revision, operating conditions and source before using a specification. Course examples are teaching fixtures. Document the physical work you perform, your inspection measurements and any specialist operations. Preserve relevant emissions controls, required safety equipment and diagnostic functions. Determine requirements for the specific intended use and jurisdiction before committing to changes.

### Frame rail

**Function.** Transfers suspension and body loads through the vehicle.

**Design.** Choose section, material, load path, fatigue detail and corrosion protection.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Cut/fixture a supervised teaching section or build to an engineered released drawing.

**Verify.** Survey datums and inspect joints to reviewed acceptance criteria.

### Crossmember

**Function.** Connects rails and supports concentrated loads.

**Design.** Define mounting reactions, local reinforcement and clearance.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Fixture a reviewed design, attach along specified nodes and protect joints.

**Verify.** Measure diagonals, pickup coordinates and resulting distortion.

### Subframe

**Function.** Positions suspension or powertrain relative to the body.

**Design.** Design attachment loads, bushing compliance, locating features and service extraction.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Install traceable donor unit or fabricate from reviewed drawings on a jig.

**Verify.** Verify locations, fastener retention, alignment and clearance.

### Bulkhead and firewall

**Function.** Separate compartments and carry loads or close penetrations.

**Design.** Plan structure, fire-resistant separation, sealing and service penetrations.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Form reviewed panels with flanges and approved sealed pass-throughs.

**Verify.** Inspect seams, cable protection and isolation of cabin from fumes.

### Floorpan and sill

**Function.** Support occupant area and contribute to body load paths.

**Design.** Design section continuity, drains, anchor reinforcement and corrosion protection.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Form/join only to the released material and joint schedule.

**Verify.** Inspect joint continuity, datum fit and drainage.

### A/B/C pillar and roof rail

**Function.** Frame door and glazing openings and contribute to occupant structure.

**Design.** Preserve approved section, joint and crash-load design.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Use qualified structural method for the exact material and location.

**Verify.** Measure aperture alignment and retain structural review.

### Gusset and doubler

**Function.** Spread localized forces into adjoining structure.

**Design.** Specify thickness transitions, load introduction and joint access.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Cut, deburr and fixture to reviewed pattern; use qualified joining method.

**Verify.** Check parent distortion, weld or fastener pattern and fit.

### Weld joint

**Function.** Joins load-bearing members by local fusion.

**Design.** Define materials, joint geometry, heat input, access and inspection criteria.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Practice on identical coupons before a qualified structural operation.

**Verify.** Document procedure, coupon outcomes and required inspection.

references.title: Primary structure, joints and attachment hardware · Through bolt to Jacking point and reinforcement
references.body:
For an actual vehicle, identify the exact model, part revision, operating conditions and source before using a specification. Course examples are teaching fixtures. Document the physical work you perform, your inspection measurements and any specialist operations. Preserve relevant emissions controls, required safety equipment and diagnostic functions. Determine requirements for the specific intended use and jurisdiction before committing to changes.

### Through bolt

**Function.** Produces clamping force or resists defined joint loading.

**Design.** Specify grade, grip, engagement, coating and tightening method.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Fit traceable bolt and correct mating nut or insert with specified lubricant conditions.

**Verify.** Record identity, measured tightening and post-test disposition.

### Threaded insert or weld nut

**Function.** Provides a serviceable thread in a panel or member.

**Design.** Choose load class, base thickness, anti-rotation and process.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Set insert in a specified hole or install weld nut using the qualified procedure.

**Verify.** Check seating, thread condition and required pull-out or torque evidence.

### Washer or load-spreading plate

**Function.** Distributes clamp load or locates a joint.

**Design.** Specify hardness, diameter, thickness and exact bearing surface.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Install the documented type in the correct stack order.

**Verify.** Verify count, orientation and seating at each location.

### Locating dowel

**Function.** Positions mating parts repeatably.

**Design.** Choose controlled fit, positional tolerance and insertion depth.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Ream matched datums where specified and press the approved dowel.

**Verify.** Check protrusion, registration and repeatability after reassembly.

### Rivet

**Function.** Joins sheet through shank loading and clamp.

**Design.** Match grip range, material, head, access and designed joint pattern.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Prepare holes and set the specified rivet using approved tooling.

**Verify.** Inspect set head, coverage, joint closure and corrosion isolation.

### Bondline adhesive

**Function.** Transfers load or seals between prepared surfaces.

**Design.** Choose product, substrate, bond gap, cure and peel control.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Prepare surfaces and apply and cure per product and vehicle procedure.

**Verify.** Record batch, cure conditions and coupon or joint inspection.

### Tow or recovery eye

**Function.** Provides a defined vehicle recovery load path.

**Design.** Identify rated direction, capacity and structural attachment.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Fit a designed, rated eye to an approved attachment.

**Verify.** Verify engagement, clearance and load documentation.

### Jacking point and reinforcement

**Function.** Carry local lifting load into the structure.

**Design.** Design or identify load path, contact geometry and stand locations.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Install only to approved structure, marking lifting and support points separately.

**Verify.** Obtain structural review and confirm accessible, stable support provisions.

references.title: Mounting and underbody protection · Stud and captive nut to Skid plate
references.body:
For an actual vehicle, identify the exact model, part revision, operating conditions and source before using a specification. Course examples are teaching fixtures. Document the physical work you perform, your inspection measurements and any specialist operations. Preserve relevant emissions controls, required safety equipment and diagnostic functions. Determine requirements for the specific intended use and jurisdiction before committing to changes.

### Stud and captive nut

**Function.** Provide retained mounting threads where rear access is limited.

**Design.** Choose base material, thread, weld or mechanical retention and expected load.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Fit by approved process on a coupon before the released panel.

**Verify.** Check thread gauge, position, anti-rotation and designed retention.

### Harness bracket

**Function.** Locates a protected wiring branch relative to moving parts.

**Design.** Set hole spacing, stand-off, bend radius, edge distance and vibration support.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Template a nonstructural bracket, cut/deburr, bend and fit retained clip.

**Verify.** Inspect clearance and inspect again after shaker or use cycles.

### Battery tray

**Function.** Provides a stable mounting base for the auxiliary battery.

**Design.** Check mass, retention path, acid/heat compatibility, drainage and post clearance.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Install approved donor tray or structurally reviewed replacement with hold-down.

**Verify.** Verify battery and tray retention and protected terminals.

### Skid plate

**Function.** Protects selected underbody components from limited impacts.

**Design.** Define intended loads, mounts, ground clearance, cooling and serviceability.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Use reviewed plate and designed load-bearing mounting points.

**Verify.** Check clearance before and after test and review any transferred impact load.

references.title: Modification · Bolt-on chassis brace
references.body:
**Purpose.** Seek a measurable reduction in deflection at a defined load path.

**Design and baseline.** Identify loaded nodes and measure initial deflection. Size brace, end fittings and parent structure against reviewed loads, fatigue and adjacent crash or service spaces.

**Build and installation.** Model brackets in card, fixture the teaching brace, build coupons using intended process and trial-fit on a reviewed noncritical bay. Use qualified design evidence for any vehicle structural attachment.

**Test and disposition.** Repeat the same supported-bay load/deflection test and inspect joints. Discard or redesign if parent structure distorts or service access disappears.

references.body:
**Purpose.** Improve debris protection, maintenance access or airflow management.

**Design and baseline.** Set requirements for drainage, engine heat, ground clearance, tire envelope, loads and removal; value aero claims only against measurements.

**Build and installation.** Make a full-size card pattern from chassis datums, transfer and cut suitable sheet, form stiffening bends, remove sharp edges and attach to reviewed supports with retained hardware.

**Test and disposition.** Check full steer/travel, heat, ground clearance, repeated removal and fastener security. Validate any aerodynamic or cooling claim separately.

For an actual vehicle, identify the exact model, part revision, operating conditions and source before using a specification. Course examples are teaching fixtures. Document the physical work you perform, your inspection measurements and any specialist operations. Preserve relevant emissions controls, required safety equipment and diagnostic functions. Determine requirements for the specific intended use and jurisdiction before committing to changes.

references.title: How to account for every installed part
references.body:
# Build-specific parts reconciliation

The teaching atlas lists common light-vehicle parts and service assemblies across multiple architectures. A gasoline manual, a diesel automatic and a battery-electric car have different inventories. The as-built bill of materials establishes what **your particular car** contains, down to separately installed hardware. Start with the actual model year, market, engine, transmission, option codes and donor/source identity. Mark privacy-sensitive paperwork for private instructor review.

1. Make a system tree for the exact vehicle. Give each parent assembly an ID. Identify the source of every child from a dated OEM parts catalog or exploded figure, engineering drawing, kit packing list, supplier specification, harness diagram or direct teardown. A commercial catalog is good for identity and fitment. Use separate authoritative service data for torque, installation and test limits. For original parts, assign drawing numbers and revisions yourself.
2. Start a line in As-Built-BOM.csv for each **part at each installation position**, including each clip, washer, spacer, seal, terminal, retainer, ground strap, hose end, fluid charge, service label and replacement-only fastener. Split left/right, front/rear, orientation and hardware stack order; link each to its parent. A separate serialized component gets its own instance. Account for consumables retained on the finished part, e.g. coating or sealant by product, batch and measured or specified amount where applicable. Mark discarded assembly aids separately.
3. Tie every row to an approved configuration. Record exact part/revision, the number or amount required, received or made, installed and independently verified, with units. Compare numbers at that installation position; purchased spare stock belongs to inventory, not installed quantity. Add any part missing from the teaching atlas. Mark a nonapplicable teaching family with the architecture-specific reason. A missing source entry is an open item.
4. Distinguish **make** (original or drawing-controlled part), **assemble** (purchased parts you personally integrated), **buy** (approved component) and **specialist** (named service or operation). Record material, tooling, process, measured features or supplier documents and who inspected it. Document critical work before it is hidden. Preserve service access and replace-only rules.
5. For a sealed bought assembly with no serviceable internal list, identify its make, model, revision or serial where available, supplier and functional boundary. List every separately fitted connector, seal, mount and fastener. If the manufacturer publishes a serviceable breakdown or you rebuild it, expand the children you actually service. Leave inaccessible internal details marked as supplier-controlled. Do not dismantle restraint inflators or sealed traction assemblies for an inventory exercise.
6. Reconcile from both directions. Walk each drawing callout into the build ledger, then walk each real installed item back to a drawing, receipt, material record or revision. Have a second person inspect quantities, location, retention and test evidence. Mark each row accepted, absent by design, awaiting evidence, rework or spare. Release a function only when all its relevant rows and measured acceptance tests have passed. Record who accepted the change. The complete car still requires the existing witnessed commissioning demonstration and its intended-use approvals.

## Worked example

The SP-01 removable-plate fixture drawing calls for one plate and one fastener/washer stack at each of two identified positions. Its practice board supplies tapped holes. The separate example CSV includes eight rows. They identify the board, the plate, two labeled mounting positions as parent groups, and the two screws and two washers distributed under those groups. Parent groups carry no physical quantities. A missing right washer is an intentional open finding. Correct the installed count only after fitting the washer; update verified count only after reinspection. Accepting the measured board and plate as individual parts leaves fixture release on hold until the corrected right stack is verified. An unused spare remains a stock item.

## Graduation review

Turn in the assembly tree, marked exploded views, drawing revisions, actual bill of materials, inspection evidence, change records and final service schedule. Account for every called-out or observed item and every receiving/installation discrepancy. An instructor must be able to pick an item on the physical car, identify who made or fitted it, locate its source or released drawing, and see how it passed the appropriate acceptance check. A passing written exam cannot certify workmanship, registration, emissions compliance or crashworthiness.

references.title: Make a removable two-hole service plate
references.body:
**Objective.** Make a non-load-bearing cover for a flat scrap practice board. Its two mounting holes must register on existing threaded bench-fixture holes, and a second person must be able to remove and refit it with the specified hand tool. This teaches how to set datums, lay out a part, select hardware and reconcile every installed item.

**Drawing SP-01, revision A.** For the exercise use 1.0 mm formable aluminum sheet, two M4 machine screws, two plain washers and two M4 threaded fixture positions 40.0 mm apart. Select screw length for the actual board/support stack without bottoming or breaking through into a hazard. A tapped practice board or two secured nuts may provide the female threads. Record the version you actually use.

| Feature | Dimension or acceptance condition |
|---|---|
| Outer rectangle | 70.0 × 35.0 mm, ±0.5 mm each direction |
| Datum A | Bottom long edge viewed from marked face |
| Datum B | Left short edge viewed from marked face |
| Left hole center | 15.0 ±0.3 mm from B, 17.5 ±0.3 mm from A |
| Right hole center | 40.0 ±0.5 mm to the right of the left hole, 17.5 ±0.3 mm from A |
| Both through holes | 4.5 mm nominal, exercise acceptance 4.4–4.7 mm |
| Finish and fit | Broken/deburred edges, clearance to hardware, both screws start by hand without moving either threaded position, cover removes and refits three times |

1. Measure the board, actual threaded-hole spacing, screw major diameter, washer outside diameter, stack and tool envelope. Make and label a card template from the two datums. If the board differs from the drawing, record a revision before cutting.
2. Mark stock and hole centers using square and rule or height gauge. Cut oversize with suitable sheet tools and finish to the outline. Clamp thin sheet flat to a sacrificial backer for drilling, use eye protection and keep hands clear of the tool. Use safe chip removal and shop-approved tooling.
3. Drill the two holes, deburr both faces, radius sharp corners and mark the datum face. Use equal, close-fitting gauge pins of known diameter in measured holes of comparable diameter, or a suitable center-measuring tool. For the equal-pin method, outside-over-pins minus one pin diameter estimates center spacing. Account for pin-to-hole clearance and instrument uncertainty. If the resulting interval crosses a limit, remeasure with a more suitable method.
4. Assemble left and right M4 screws with one specified washer at each position. If using separate nuts, add both as individual bill-of-materials instances. Verify clearance on the underside of the board and that hardware does not bottom out. Cycle removal and refit three times.
5. Compare as-built numbers against the drawing. Example inspection: with two 4.49 mm pins in 4.50 mm holes, an outside measurement of 44.69 mm estimates 40.20 mm center spacing. With estimated total uncertainty ±0.03 mm the complete interval is inside the specified spacing range; it cannot prove hole diameter or edge position. Check those separately.

**Fresh assignment.** A supplied teaching board has holes 52.0 mm apart. Design a new cover which keeps the left datum and comparable edge margins, document a new overall length and right-hole location, make it and have another learner inspect it. Submit the drawing, finished sample, actual readings and bill of materials. A disproportionate or slotted second hole to hide an error requires a documented design change.

writing.title: Draw a chassis bay and its fixture
writing.prompt: Choose a bay from a documented design or a chassis engineer's reviewed concept. Mark three datums, simple load paths, wheel and seat reference locations, tolerances, tool access and a fixture inspection sequence. Identify where the structural reviewer must approve the proposed use. Include a labeled drawing or table in the work record and identify the applicable shop or legal requirement.

writing.title: Component selection and evidence
writing.prompt: For this course examine Primary chassis; Material and structural joint; Mounts and fasteners. Identify each applicable family on your own vehicle or donor and explain absent families. Use two identified alternatives for at least one consequential choice. Show the job each design performs, how its operating principle differs, one failure mode and a test that separates the alternatives. Identify a real model or part number for each shortlisted candidate. Compare a sourced limit or performance figure under common conditions, interfaces, legal or shop implications and service access. Defend your choice and explain one change that would reverse it. Link your drawing and physical observation or measurement to the build record.

writing.title: Workshop record · Make a drawing someone else can inspect
writing.prompt: Make the two-hole nonstructural service plate in the bench plans, log each manufactured and purchased part, and test removal and refit. List your donor or drawing revision, part identities, position, material or rating, method, who made or fitted each item, and the governing source. State the goal, the baseline test, a controlled change, a potential adverse effect, comparable measured results, acceptance threshold and rollback. Include an attributable photograph, recorded direct observation or measurement. An inert prototype or mock-up qualifies for this comparison exercise when the vehicle modification requires specialist or legal approval. Identify exactly which vehicle results are still unproven.

labs.title: Fabricate and inspect a representative chassis bay
labs.intro: A fabricated bay, its jig, inspected coupons and an as-built dimensional report. Plan shop time with your supervisor over the sessions the work actually takes.
safety: Only weld under a qualified shop's hot-work controls with appropriate local exhaust, PPE and fire precautions. Never weld on containers or structures with fuel or unknown residues. Keep prototype parts out of vehicle use until reviewed.
materials: Equipped supervised welding shop and representative coupons
steps: Make the fixture and document datum checks. Fit the cut members and retain labeled material records.
Practice on representative coupons and record the welding instructor's disposition.
Fabricate the bay to the reviewed work instruction. Measure it at tack stage and again when cool.
Have the bay inspected against its drawing. Record every deviation and disposition before adopting the process for the car.

questions.prompt: What did you personally make or service? Record actual conditions, measured values, instruments, and any specialist operations.

The physically fabricated bay, coupon record and datum-based measurements can be traced to one drawing revision. Record your result, corrections, retest and sign-off status. Include the witness name and date where required.
Which rule, authority or shop control applied at this site? Identify the actor, triggering operation, source and the record kept.

Name the actual part or trainer component and the design alternative you considered. Record the observed or measured result, units and conditions where applicable, and its effect on the as-built decision.
Identify one fitted part and each fastener, seal, clip or connector that you personally handled. Record parent assembly, position, source, required and observed quantity, and evidence.

labs.photos: Attach dated photographs of your own work, with part or revision identification. An instructor may also document direct observation.
